newsitem.title: FINLAND: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA FORCE THIRD GAME.
newsitem.headline: ICE HOCKEY-CANADA FORCE THIRD GAME.

text.p: Canada beat Olympic champions Sweden 3-1 on Tuesday to force a deciding game in the best-of- three gold medal final at the ice hockey world championships.
Canada's gritty performance has set up a winner-take-all grudge match on Wednesday against the team that beat them in an overtime shootout in Lillehammer to win the gold medal.
"We didn't come up to our normal level, it was quite difficult to play because we already had one victory and we knew we didn't have to play for our lives," said Sweden coach Kent Forsberg.
Canada got second period goals through Geoff Sanderson and Anson Carter then rode the goaltending of Hartford Whalers Sean Burke to force a decisive third game.

"All the players were confident," said Canadian coach Andy Murray, who gave his team yesterday off and instead conducted half-hour one-on-one meetings with each player to prepare them for the game. "They knew going into this you had to win two games and that was still the same situation after we lost the first one.
"We have to win a couple of hockey games within 27 hours.
"We just have to make sure we're ready to go."

Burke, who has started every game of the tournament in the Canadian net, was at his acrobatic best in the key third period, making back-to-back saves, including a breakaway by Swedish sniper Michael Nylander, to preserve Canada's lead.
"I like to have the chance to make a big save and I was happy I was able to do that tonight," said Burke. "I think we're hungry for this.
"When you don't make the NHL playoffs you feel like a loser.
"This is a chance to go home this summer feeling like a winner."

In a scoreless first period Canada were able to avoid the costly penalties that led to a 3-2 defeat in game one but continued to be frustrated by New York Islander goaltender Tommy Salo in the Sweden net.
Canada outshot the Swedes 14-8 but were unable to beat the all-star netminder until midway through the second when Sanderson broke out of an eight game scoring slump to give them a 1-0 lead.
Travis Green set up the goal as he swung around behind the Sweden net and snapped a wristshot off Salo's mask, the puck deflecting in off Sanderson's stick.
Less than two minutes later Sweden levelled the score on a powerplay by Per Eklund.
Carter sent Canada into the second intermission up 2-1 when the Boston Bruin centre took a return pass from Chris Gratton and slapped it into the empty net.
Montreal Canadiens Mark Recchi added an insurance goal early in the third when his weak wrist shot, drifted between Salo's pads.
The game ended with referee Gerhard Muller fighting to retain control of the contest as tempers flared.
The two teams refused to shake hands as is the custom after an international match.
"Some the Canadian were making bad gestures while the Swedish player was getting his award for being the best player after the match," said Forsberg, "That's why we refused to shake hands."
